Spot Bitcoin ETFs Saw $229 Million in Net Outflows Last Week, While Spot Ethereum ETFs Recorded $320 Million From October 12 to 16 (ET), spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of $229 million, led by BlackRock’s IBIT with $165 million. Spot Ethereum ETFs recorded net outflows of $320 million, marking their third consecutive week of net outflows. — link

JPMorgan to Offer JPM Coin Deposit Token to Institutional Clients on Ethereum According to Bloomberg, JPMorgan announced that it will offer its JPM Coin deposit token to institutional clients on Ethereum, enabling round-the-clock payments that settle in seconds. The token represents clients’ U.S. dollar deposits at JPMorgan and first launched on Base last year. It is expected to support on-chain payments for large clients in the crypto sector, as well as settlement or collateralization of tokenized asset transactions by financial institutions. — link

Upbit to List CT Trading Pairs Against KRW, BTC, and USDT According to an official announcement, Upbit, South Korea’s largest crypto exchange, will list CT trading pairs against KRW, BTC, and USDT. Trading is scheduled to begin on October 19 at 18:00 (KST). Concrete is an on-chain asset management infrastructure project, and CT is used for governance and staking. — link

BNB Chain burns 1.65M BNB worth about $1B in 37th quarterly auto-burn BNB Chain completed its 37th quarterly BNB Auto-Burn, removing about 1.646 million BNB worth roughly $1 billion at the reference price. The Auto-Burn mechanism determines the amount based on BNB’s price and the number of BNB Smart Chain blocks produced during the quarter, with the long-term goal of reducing total BNB supply to 100 million. BNB Chain also continues to burn a portion of gas fees through BEP-95. — link
